title: Monday Morning Quarterback

paragraphs: This is the NFL Week 7 recap: Thursday night and Sunday, 13 finals. Every pick is graded against the line printed on its card at kickoff. When a handicapper changed a pick at Lock It Up, the changed pick is the one that counts, and we tell you how the original would have done. A push counts as neither a hit nor a miss. Buffalo, the Chargers, Washington and Jacksonville were off this week, and Dallas at Philadelphia on Monday night gets graded in next week's edition. Each recap starts with the card, then rides along with the tickets: the number each side and the total needed, the plays and flags that swung them, then who called it and who missed it.

Follow The Money only picks when the number moves by a point or more, so it sat out most of the week and made one call, on a total. In The Trenches only plays where the line of scrimmage tells it something, and this week it had something to say on every game.

College already got its full recap in the Oct. 24 edition, so here is just the reminder. The Cover Writer went 25-30-1 against the spread and 25-31 on totals in college last week, and the push was Indiana −7 in a 13-6 overtime win at Michigan. Everybody's full college numbers are in that edition.

Card line: Bears −3, total 50.5. The Cover Writer's card had the Patriots +3 and the Under 50.5, projecting Patriots 24, Bears 22. Final: Bears 30, Patriots 24. The Bears won by 6, and the teams scored 54 points.

Patriots +3 meant New England could lose by two and still get paid, and every picker who plays sides had that ticket in a shirt pocket. Chicago went up 10-0, and Drake Maye's 7-yard touchdown scramble only counted after New England challenged and won. Then the second quarter got loud. Maye threw an interception to D'Marco Jackson in the end zone at 3:32, and a roughing-the-passer flag on New England's Gabe Jacas tacked 15 yards onto Chicago's next drive. With 14 seconds left in the half Caleb Williams hit Luther Burden III for a 24-yard touchdown, and Maye answered on the last play of the half with a 48-yarder to Rhamondre Stevenson. Down six at the break, the +3 was alive. Maye's 30-yard touchdown to Eli Raridon at 3:46 of the third made it 27-21, and the Patriots +3 crowd needed one more stop and one more score.

The stop came, and so did the heartbreak. Cairo Santos clanked a 53-yarder off the right upright at 8:02 of the fourth, which kept New England within six and left the Under 50.5 sitting pretty at 48 points. At 1:34 Santos came back out from 58 and drilled it. That made it 30-21, put 51 on the board and beat the Under by half a point in one swing. Andy Borregales hit from 47 with 37 seconds left, which got the Patriots within six, a field goal short of a push. Williams took a knee at 0:36, and every ticket in the group project lost together. The Formula's review of the night is one sentence long: the kicker who missed from 53 made it from 58, and the Under is still asking for an explanation.

Missed: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Patriots +3, missed by 3 points. The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Under 50.5, went over by 3.5 points.
No pick: Follow The Money on the side or the total.

Card line: Steelers −3.5, total 44.5. The Cover Writer's card had the Steelers −3.5 and the Over 44.5, projecting Steelers 26, Saints 22. Final: Steelers 16, Saints 10. The Steelers won by 6, and the teams scored 26 points.

Steelers −3.5 needed a four-point win in Paris, and the Saints +3.5 needed anything less. Chris Boswell kicked from 28, Aaron Rodgers found Darnell Washington for a 4-yard touchdown, and Tyler Shough tied it at 10 with a 1-yard touchdown pass to Devaughn Vele on 4th-and-goal. Boswell's 47-yarder at the end of the half made it 13-10, a three-point lead, which is the one number nobody holding −3.5 wants to see. Payton Wilson intercepted Shough at the Pittsburgh 11, and Boswell's 39-yarder late in the third made it 16-10. Now the Steelers were covering by 2.5. Daniel Carlson lined up a 52-yarder at 9:32 of the fourth that would have made it a three-point game and flipped the cover to the Saints, and he pushed it wide right.

Boswell made one more from 37 at 1:04, and it came off the board because New Orleans' Stalbird lined up offside. That handed Pittsburgh a first down, and Rodgers knelt twice to finish it. The Cover Writer, The Formula and Letdown Watch thanked Stalbird for his service. The Over 44.5 was in trouble by halftime at 23 points, and the second half added three. Even the 37-yarder that got wiped out would only have made it 29. All five pickers who play totals had the Over, and all five would like a refund on the trip to France.
Called it: The Cover Writer, The Formula and Letdown Watch on the Steelers −3.5, covered by 2.5 points.

Missed: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Over 44.5, fell short by 18.5 points. Next Man Up and In The Trenches on the Saints +3.5, missed by 2.5 points.
No pick: Follow The Money on the side or the total.

Card line: 49ers −3.5, total 50.5. The Cover Writer's card had the 49ers −3.5 and the Under 50.5, projecting 49ers 27, Falcons 21. Final: Falcons 29, 49ers 20. The Falcons won by 9, and the teams scored 49 points.

Five pickers laid the 49ers −3.5, which needed a four-point win, and for a quarter and change it looked like money. Christian McCaffrey scored from a yard out, and Kaelon Black ran 30 yards for a touchdown early in the second quarter to make it 14-3. Then Michael Penix Jr. took over. He hit Nick Muse for a touchdown, Nick Folk kicked a 33-yarder on the last play of the half, and Penix threw touchdowns to Kyle Pitts Sr. and Drake London, the last a 21-yarder early in the fourth for a 26-14 lead. In between, Jessie Bates III intercepted Brock Purdy at the Atlanta 10. San Francisco thought it had a 23-yard touchdown to Jordan Watkins, and replay reversed it. Purdy's 1-yard touchdown to Kyle Juszczyk at 5:05 made it 26-20, and 49ers −3.5 holders started doing math. Kendal Daniels ended the math at 2:42 with an interception and a 29-yard return, and Folk's 31-yard field goal made it 29-20.

The Under 50.5 was a story about extra points. Folk's kick after the Muse touchdown hit the right upright, and Eddy Pineiro pushed his wide left after the Juszczyk touchdown. Make both and the total is 51, half a point over. The Under had one last scare at 0:57, when George Kittle caught a 22-yarder down to the Atlanta 19 and Bates knocked it loose for Daniels to recover. Penix knelt three times, and the game finished at 49, a point and a half under. Follow The Money only plays when the number moves, it moved onto the Over, and two missed extra points did it in. Every Under ticket owes both kickers a fruit basket.
Called it: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Under 50.5, stayed under by 1.5 points.
Missed: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the 49ers −3.5, missed by 12.5 points. Follow The Money on the Over 50.5, fell short by 1.5 points.
No pick: Follow The Money on the side.

Card line: Browns −1.5, total 38.5. The Cover Writer's card had the Titans +1.5 and the Under 38.5, projecting Browns 19, Titans 18. Final: Browns 27, Titans 24. The Browns won by 3, and the teams scored 51 points.

Titans +1.5 cashes on a tie or a one-point loss, so for most of the fourth quarter four pickers were rooting for overtime. Tony Pollard scored from 36 and from 10 yards in the first quarter, and a third Pollard touchdown in the second quarter came back on replay with the ball at the 1. Cleveland led 17-14 at the half after Andre Szmyt's 28-yarder. Szmyt clanked a 43-yarder off the right upright early in the fourth, Joey Slye tied it at 17 from 29 yards, and Deshaun Watson's 9-yard touchdown run at 4:34 put Cleveland up seven. Pollard went in from a yard out with 58 seconds left to tie it 24-24, and the Titans +1.5 was covering. Then, with three seconds left and Cleveland lining up a kick from the 19, Tennessee's Williams jumped offside. Szmyt hit from 32 on the final play. Tennessee lost by three, the four pickers on the Titans +1.5 lost by a point and a half, and Letdown Watch, alone on the Browns −1.5, is being insufferable about it.

The Under 38.5 was in trouble by halftime. The teams had 31 points at the break, so the Under needed the second half to produce seven points or fewer. Szmyt's miss off the upright helped. Slye's field goal made it 34, and Watson's touchdown at 4:34 of the fourth made it 41 and ended the Under. Next Man Up and In The Trenches had the Over, and they spent the last four minutes relaxing.
Called it: Next Man Up and In The Trenches on the Over 38.5, cleared it by 12.5 points. Letdown Watch on the Browns −1.5, covered by 1.5 points.

Missed: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up and In The Trenches on the Titans +1.5, missed by 1.5 points. The Cover Writer, The Formula and Letdown Watch on the Under 38.5, went over by 12.5 points.
No pick: Follow The Money on the side or the total.

Card line: Vikings −6.5, total 41.5. The Cover Writer's card had the Colts +6.5 and the Over 41.5, projecting Vikings 24, Colts 19. Final: Vikings 16, Colts 10. The Vikings won by 6, and the teams scored 26 points.

Colts +6.5 needed Indianapolis to lose by six or fewer, and the fourth quarter was one long held breath. Jonathan Taylor's 38-yard touchdown run and Spencer Shrader's 43-yarder at the end of the half had the Colts up 10-6, and T.J. Hockenson's 5-yard touchdown catch early in the fourth put Minnesota up 13-10. Grover Stewart blocked Will Reichard's 59-yard try at 8:38. Shrader missed from 48 at 4:27, which would have tied it. Then the big one. With 2:02 left Kyler Murray hit Jordan Addison for 34 yards down to the Colts' 2, and a holding call on Minnesota's Brandel wiped it out. A touchdown there and the Colts +6.5 is dead. The Vikings settled for Reichard's 52-yard field goal at 1:39 and a six-point lead, Harrison Smith intercepted Daniel Jones at 1:15, and Murray knelt it out. The Colts +6.5 cashed by half a point, and Letdown Watch, on the Vikings −6.5, would like that flag reviewed by Congress.

The Over 41.5 never got going. The teams had 16 points at halftime, so the Over needed 26 in the second half. It got 10. Shrader missed from 56 and 48, and Stewart's block took three more off the board. In The Trenches went Under by itself and was the only one in the group chat who didn't need a nap.
Called it: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up and In The Trenches on the Colts +6.5, covered by 0.5 points. In The Trenches on the Under 41.5, stayed under by 15.5 points.
Missed: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up and Letdown Watch on the Over 41.5, fell short by 15.5 points. Letdown Watch on the Vikings −6.5, missed by 0.5 points.
No pick: Follow The Money on the side or the total.

Card line: Jets −4.5, total 39.5. The Cover Writer's card had the Dolphins +4.5 and the Over 39.5, projecting Jets 23, Dolphins 19. Final: Dolphins 28, Jets 25. The Dolphins won by 3, and the teams scored 53 points.

Jets −4.5 needed a five-point win, and the Dolphins +4.5 just needed to keep it close. Miami did better than that. Malik Willis hit Caleb Douglas for a 7-yard touchdown in the first quarter, Michael Taaffe intercepted Geno Smith early in the second quarter, and Willis scrambled in from 2 yards with six seconds left in the half for a 21-7 lead. Jason Sanders missed a 40-yarder off the right upright for the Jets in the third, but Omar Cooper Jr.'s 3-yard touchdown catch and Sanders' 33-yard field goal at 8:57 of the fourth got New York within 21-17. Jets −4.5 holders needed one touchdown and one stop. Instead Willis hit Douglas for a 63-yard touchdown at 4:44, and it was 28-17. The Jets scored at 3:24 on Smith's 12-yard touchdown pass to Mason Taylor, had their first two-point conversion wiped out by an illegal shift on Taylor, and converted the do-over from farther back. That made it 28-25, and Willis knelt twice to end it. The Formula and In The Trenches laid the 4.5 with New York, and New York politely declined.

The Over 39.5 had 28 points at halftime and then went to sleep. Cooper's touchdown made it 35, and Sanders' field goal made it 38, still a point and a half short with under nine minutes left. Douglas's 63-yard touchdown took the total from 38 to 45 in one play, and the Jets' touchdown and two-point try ran it to 53. All five pickers who play totals had the Over and cashed it by 13.5.

Called it: The Cover Writer, Next Man Up and Letdown Watch on the Dolphins +4.5, covered by 7.5 points. The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Over 39.5, cleared it by 13.5 points.
Missed: The Formula and In The Trenches on the Jets −4.5, missed by 7.5 points.
No pick: Follow The Money on the side or the total.

Card line: Panthers −3.5, total 44.5. The Cover Writer's card had the Panthers −3.5 and the Over 44.5, projecting Panthers 26, Buccaneers 21. Final: Buccaneers 43, Panthers 13. The Buccaneers won by 30, and the teams scored 56 points.

Panthers −3.5 needed a four-point home win off a win in Philadelphia, and Carolina got run over instead. Yaya Diaby sacked Bryce Young early in the second quarter. On the very next snap Al-Quadin Muhammad sacked Young and knocked the ball loose, and Calijah Kancey returned it 32 yards for a touchdown. When Darren Waller finally got the Panthers into the end zone with a 50-yard catch, Ryan Fitzgerald's extra point was blocked and Zyon McCollum returned it for two points the other way. McCollum later intercepted Young. A Chris Godwin Jr. touchdown came back on an illegal shift, and Baker Mayfield simply threw a 14-yard touchdown to Tez Johnson with four seconds left in the half instead. It was 33-6 at the break, and the −3.5 needed a 31-point second half. Diaby added two more sacks to open the third. Four pickers laid the points with the Panthers and lost by 33.5. Next Man Up was alone on the Buccaneers +3.5 and is accepting congratulations in writing.

The Over 44.5 had 39 points at halftime and needed six more. Chase McLaughlin's 44-yard field goal in the third got it to 42, and Sean Tucker's 46-yard touchdown run at 10:21 of the fourth made it 49 and cashed it. Anthony Tyus III added a 12-yard touchdown for Carolina at 5:28, which helped nobody except the Over's margin. In The Trenches had the Under and watched the Tampa Bay defense score a touchdown and a two-point return by itself.
Called it: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up and Letdown Watch on the Over 44.5, cleared it by 11.5 points. Next Man Up on the Buccaneers +3.5, covered by 33.5 points.
Missed: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Panthers −3.5, missed by 33.5 points. In The Trenches on the Under 44.5, went over by 11.5 points.
No pick: Follow The Money on the side or the total.

Card line: Ravens −2.5, total 51. The Cover Writer's card had the Ravens −2.5 and the Under 51, projecting Ravens 26, Bengals 23. Final: Bengals 35, Ravens 13. The Bengals won by 22, and the teams scored 48 points.

This is the Lock It Up game, and Lock It Up would like it struck from the record. Baltimore ruled Lamar Jackson out on Saturday, the number swung from Baltimore −2.5 to Baltimore +3 by Sunday morning, and Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches left the Bengals +2.5 for the Ravens +3. For one half everyone holding a Baltimore ticket looked brilliant. Tyler Huntley's 48-yard touchdown pass to Zay Flowers and Tyler Loop field goals from 34 and 24 made it 13-0. Then Joe Burrow went to work: a 6-yard touchdown to Mike Gesicki and a 13-yarder to Tee Higgins at 4:29 of the third for a 14-13 lead. The Ravens −2.5 was now losing, and the Ravens +3 was still alive. A pass interference flag on Baltimore's K'Von Wallace set up Samaje Perine's 1-yard touchdown run, and that ended the +3 too. Burrow added a 2-yarder to Ja'Marr Chase, Demetrius Knight Jr. intercepted Huntley, and Drew Sample caught a 16-yard touchdown at 6:21. The side change turned a 24.5-point winner into a 19-point loser, and the three pickers who made it are not taking questions.

The total was the fun part. The Cover Writer had the Under 51, and the four movers had the Over 46.5, so the dream was 47, 48, 49 or 50. It was 13 at halftime. Chase's touchdown made it 41, and Sample's touchdown at 6:21 made it 48, past the 46.5 and still under the 51. Then everybody held their breath for six minutes and twenty-one seconds, and nobody scored again. Both tickets cashed. Everybody agrees this is the only part of the game worth discussing.
Called it: The Cover Writer on the Under 51, stayed under by 3 points. The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Over 46.5, cleared it by 1.5 points.
Missed: The Cover Writer and The Formula on the Ravens −2.5, missed by 24.5 points. Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Ravens +3, missed by 19 points.

Lock It Up check: The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches moved off the Under 51 to the Over 46.5, and the Under 51 would have stayed under by 3 points. Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches moved off the Bengals +2.5 to the Ravens +3, and the Bengals +2.5 would have covered by 24.5 points.
No pick: Follow The Money on the side or the total.

Card line: Texans −9.5, total 43. The Cover Writer's card had the Giants +9.5 and the Over 43, projecting Texans 26, Giants 18. Final: Giants 27, Texans 21 in overtime. The Giants won by 6, and the teams scored 48 points.

Giants +9.5 meant New York could lose by nine and still cash, and the Giants never needed a single one of those points. Ka'imi Fairbairn hit from 58 and 57 for Houston, and Dominic Zvada missed from 56 for the Giants. Houston tied it 14-14 with 34 seconds left in the half on a 6-yard touchdown pass and a two-point conversion, and Zvada then missed from 44. The Giants' Ar'Darius Washington thought he had a 41-yard fumble-return touchdown in the third quarter, and replay took it back. Cam Skattebo's 16-yard touchdown run at 8:55 of the fourth put New York up 21-14, and C.J. Stroud tied it with a 3-yard touchdown to Xavier Hutchinson with 52 seconds left. Devin Singletary ran 30 yards for the winning touchdown in overtime. The Formula gets credit for its Lock It Up move from the Texans −9.5 to the Giants +10.5, which turned a loss into a win by 16.5.

The total of 43 was the real sweat. It was 28 at halftime, Skattebo's touchdown made it 35, and Hutchinson's touchdown made it 42. Regulation ended 21-21, one point under 43, and In The Trenches had the Under. One overtime stop would have done it. Singletary's touchdown ended the game 27-21, and the total finished at 48. Overtime counts, and In The Trenches has filed a formal complaint about that.

Called it: The Cover Writer, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Giants +9.5, covered by 15.5 points. The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up and Letdown Watch on the Over 43, cleared it by 5 points. The Formula on the Giants +10.5, covered by 16.5 points.
Missed: In The Trenches on the Under 43, went over by 5 points.
Lock It Up check: The Formula moved off the Texans −9.5 to the Giants +10.5, and the Texans −9.5 would have missed by 15.5 points.
No pick: Follow The Money on the side or the total.

Card line: Broncos −4.5, total 43.5. The Cover Writer's card had the Cardinals +4.5 and the Over 43.5, projecting Broncos 24, Cardinals 20. Final: Broncos 30, Cardinals 16. The Broncos won by 14, and the teams scored 46 points.

Cardinals +4.5 needed Arizona within four, and Bo Nix took that personally. It was 6-6 until Nix scrambled 62 yards for a touchdown before the half, and he threw a 52-yard touchdown to RJ Harvey early in the third. Trey McBride's 7-yard touchdown catch made it 20-13, and Arizona +4.5 holders were back in it, one more score from the right side. On the last play of the third J.K. Dobbins went in from a yard out, and replay upheld it. That was 27-13, and the cover was gone. Wil Lutz added a 31-yarder, Chad Ryland answered from 41, and late in the fourth Jahdae Barron was flagged for pass interference at the 1 twice in seven seconds. Alex Singleton then sacked Jacoby Brissett at the 5, and Nix knelt it out. Letdown Watch was alone on the Broncos −4.5 and has already printed the ticket.

The Over 43.5 was a nail-biter in slow motion. Lutz's 31-yarder at 8:39 of the fourth made it 30-13 and 43 points, half a point short. Then Ryland lined up a 41-yarder on 4th-and-17 at 6:21. He made it, the score went to 30-16, and 46 points beat the 43.5. In The Trenches had the Under and lost it to a field goal on 4th-and-17. Of all the ways. Barron's two flags at the goal line could have added seven more, but the Over was already home.
Called it: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up and Letdown Watch on the Over 43.5, cleared it by 2.5 points. Letdown Watch on the Broncos −4.5, covered by 9.5 points.
Missed: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up and In The Trenches on the Cardinals +4.5, missed by 9.5 points. In The Trenches on the Under 43.5, went over by 2.5 points.
No pick: Follow The Money on the side or the total.

Card line: Lions −3, total 53.5. The Cover Writer's card had the Packers +3 and the Under 53.5, projecting Lions 26, Packers 25. Final: Lions 20, Packers 17. The Lions won by 3, and the teams scored 37 points.

Lions −3 and Packers +3, with a final margin of three. Every side on this game pushed, and it took all 60 minutes to get there. Green Bay's Trey Smack missed from 26 in the first quarter, right after a Packers delay of game backed him up. Jared Goff found Jameson Williams for a 16-yard touchdown, Jordan Love hit Tucker Kraft from 14, and Jake Bates made a 40-yarder for a 10-7 Detroit halftime lead. Josh Jacobs' 25-yard touchdown catch put Green Bay up 14-10, and Goff's 10-yarder to Williams put Detroit back up 17-14. Brandon Cisse intercepted Goff at the Green Bay 11 and lost it to his own pass interference flag. Smack tied it at 17 from 43 yards, and with the score tied 17-17 DJ Wonnum blocked Smack's 35-yarder at 3:25. A make there and the Packers +3 cashes outright. Detroit's last drive picked up a Karl Brooks roughing-the-passer flag and a Brooks neutral zone infraction. Goff knelt at the Green Bay 4 with 27 seconds left, which meant Lions −3 backers watched their team choose a field goal on purpose, and Bates hit the 22-yarder at 0:00. The Packers +3 crowd gets a refund, Letdown Watch on the Lions −3 gets a refund, and nobody got anything else.

The Under 53.5 was comfortable all day. It was 17 at halftime, and Isaiah McDuffie made sure it stayed slow. He forced a Jahmyr Gibbs fumble at the Green Bay 6 before the half and recovered a Goff fumble to start the third, and Brian Branch intercepted Love early in the fourth. The teams scored 37 against a total of 53.5, and all five pickers who play totals cashed the Under by 16.5.
Called it: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Under 53.5, stayed under by 16.5 points.
Push: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up and In The Trenches on the Packers +3, landed exactly on the number. Letdown Watch on the Lions −3, landed exactly on the number.
No pick: Follow The Money on the side or the total.

Card line: Rams −4.5, total 47.5. The Cover Writer's card had the Rams −4.5 and the Over 47.5, projecting Rams 27, Raiders 22. Final: Rams 35, Raiders 21. The Rams won by 14, and the teams scored 56 points.

Rams −4.5 on the card, and Rams −3.5 for the three pickers who switched sides on Sunday morning, and Los Angeles had both tickets cashed by halftime. Matt Gay missed a 51-yarder for Las Vegas in the first quarter, and a Blake Corum touchdown came back on a holding flag. It didn't matter. Matthew Stafford threw two touchdowns to Davis Allen and one to Puka Nacua, and Kyren Williams ran in from 17 to make it 28-3. Corum's 43-yard touchdown run in the third came back too, on a face mask on the Rams' Avila. Then the Raiders made it interesting. Tre Tucker's 37-yard touchdown catch early in the fourth, Nakobe Dean's interception of Stafford on the Rams' next snap, and Ashton Jeanty's 15-yard touchdown catch at 13:12 made it 28-18. Both two-point tries failed, and the Rams −4.5 was down to a 5.5-point cushion. Corum scored from 4 at 6:34, and the sweat was over. Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches moved from the Raiders +4.5 to the Rams −3.5. The Raiders +4.5 would have lost by 9.5. The Rams −3.5 won by 10.5. Credit where it is due.

The Over 47.5 had 34 at halftime after Gay's 27-yarder on the last play of the half. Tucker's touchdown made it 40 and Jeanty's made it 46, with two failed two-point tries keeping it a point and a half short. Corum's touchdown at 6:34 made it 53, and Gay's 36-yard field goal made it 56. Stafford knelt three times to finish it. Next Man Up moved from the Over 47.5 to the Under 48.5 that morning. The Over would have cashed by 8.5, and Next Man Up will hear about it at every Lock It Up call this season. In The Trenches had the Under 47.5 from the start and has no one to blame but itself.

Called it: The Cover Writer and The Formula on the Rams −4.5, covered by 9.5 points. The Cover Writer, The Formula and Letdown Watch on the Over 47.5, cleared it by 8.5 points. Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Rams −3.5, covered by 10.5 points.
Missed: Next Man Up on the Under 48.5, went over by 7.5 points. In The Trenches on the Under 47.5, went over by 8.5 points.

Lock It Up check: Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches moved off the Raiders +4.5 to the Rams −3.5, and the Raiders +4.5 would have missed by 9.5 points. Next Man Up moved off the Over 47.5 to the Under 48.5, and the Over 47.5 would have cleared it by 8.5 points.
No pick: Follow The Money on the side or the total.

Card line: Seahawks −2.5, total 42.5. The Cover Writer's card had the Chiefs +2.5 and the Over 42.5, projecting Seahawks 23, Chiefs 21. Final: Seahawks 20, Chiefs 3. The Seahawks won by 17, and the teams scored 23 points.

Chiefs +2.5 needed Kansas City to lose by two or fewer, and Seattle's defense never let it get that close. Jason Myers kicked a 25-yarder, Ty Okada intercepted Patrick Mahomes in the second quarter, and Sam Darnold found Jaxon Smith-Njigba for a 28-yard touchdown after replay turned a step out of bounds into a score. Kansas City's best moment was Nohl Williams intercepting Darnold in the end zone and returning it 65 yards, and then Harrison Butker's 58-yard try fell short on the last play of the half. That one would have made it 10-3. Myers made it 13-0 from 35, and Butker's 50-yarder got the Chiefs to 13-3. Butker missed from 45 wide right at 8:38 of the fourth, and Emanuel Wilson's 21-yard touchdown run at 3:47 finished it. Four pickers had the Chiefs +2.5 and lost by 14.5. Letdown Watch was alone on the Seahawks −2.5 and cashed it by the same 14.5.

The Over 42.5 had 10 points at halftime and needed 33 more. It got 13. Butker's two misses took six points off a total that needed every one of them. In The Trenches had the Under and was the only one in the group chat still awake for the end.
Called it: Letdown Watch on the Seahawks −2.5, covered by 14.5 points. In The Trenches on the Under 42.5, stayed under by 19.5 points.

Missed: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up and In The Trenches on the Chiefs +2.5, missed by 14.5 points. The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up and Letdown Watch on the Over 42.5, fell short by 19.5 points.
No pick: Follow The Money on the side or the total.

hits.heading: Part 1, continued: The week's W-L and smack talk

paragraphs: Same rules as Part 1: card line at kickoff, Lock It Up changes graded as the final pick, and a push counts as neither a hit nor a miss. Here is how NFL Week 7 came out for everybody, in the usual card order, with Monday night still to play.

The Cover Writer went 5-7-1 against the spread and 8-5 on totals. The push was Green Bay at Detroit, where Jake Bates' kick on the last snap made it exactly three. The Cover Writer would like to point out that the totals paid the bills, and the Panthers −3.5 is not going on the refrigerator.

The Formula went 4-8-1 on sides and 8-5 on totals. Its original sides would have gone 3-9-1, so the Lock It Up move to the Giants +10.5 was the best thing that happened to it all weekend. It has asked that we stop mentioning the Jets.

Next Man Up went 5-7-1 on sides and 8-5 on totals. Its original picks would have gone 5-7-1 and 9-4. The Ravens and Rams side changes canceled each other out, and the move off the Rams Over cost it a total. It also had the Buccaneers +3.5 by itself, and it will be bringing that up at every Lock It Up call until Christmas.

Letdown Watch went 7-5-1 on sides and 8-5 on totals. That is a winning week on sides, built on going against the crowd in Cleveland, Denver and Seattle. Letdown Watch has already been reminded that a good Sunday is exactly how a letdown starts.
Follow The Money made no side picks and went 0-1 on totals. One call all week, the Over in Atlanta, and two missed extra points sank it. The money talked once and mumbled.

In The Trenches went 3-9-1 on sides and 7-6 on totals. It went Under alone in Minnesota and Seattle and cashed both, then went Under alone in Houston and lost it in overtime. The sides are being sent back to the line of scrimmage for more film work.

Now the smack talk. Every picker who plays sides has the Eagles +4.5 and the Over 44.5 tonight, which means either everybody is a genius by midnight or the group chat goes very quiet. Next Man Up and In The Trenches both project a Dallas win and still took the points, so they would like the Cowboys to win by exactly one, please. Letdown Watch, fresh off its best Sunday, says the Eagles win outright, and everyone else is quietly waiting for the letdown.

paragraphs: Kickoff tonight at 8:15 PM ET on ESPN, ABC and Disney+, at Lincoln Financial Field. Dallas is 2-4 and Philadelphia is 2-4. Card line: Cowboys −4.5, total 44.5, the consensus number as of 8:52 AM ET on Oct. 20. The current DraftKings number on ESPN, rechecked at 6:47 PM ET, Oct. 26, is still Cowboys −4.5 with a total of 43.5. The spread hasn't budged, and the total has dropped a point.
Cole Garrison speaks for Dallas and never confuses the brand with the results. Ray Donnelly speaks for Philadelphia and watches every snap of blocking twice.

Ray: Last week was ugly, Cole, I'll say it first. Carolina came into our building and beat us 25-14. And now ESPN says Jalen Hurts is expected to miss the rest of the season with blood clots, so it's Tanner McKee's offense.

Cole: I'm sorry about Hurts, Ray, sincerely. We lost 23-13 at Green Bay, and the game had 22 penalties, 11 by each team. CeeDee Lamb caught nine passes for 70 yards and George Pickens six for 73. The results said 2-4, and I don't argue with results.

Ray: Saquon Barkley is still questionable with the hamstring, but NFL Network's Mike Garafolo reported Monday morning that he's trending toward playing. Jonathan Greenard is questionable with an ankle and is a game-time decision. And Landon Dickerson is listed as active again after his stint on injured reserve with the knee. DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks are both out, so it's the tight end's night. Nolan Smith is out with a concussion too.

Cole: We're without KaVontae Turpin, Shelton and Winters, and Locke and Liufau were downgraded to out on Sunday. Pickens practiced fully Friday, so he's good to go. And Ray, Philadelphia runs for 3.8 yards a carry. Our defense allows 4.9. Somebody has to find a running game, and I'm not sure it's you.
Ray: Super Bowl LIX, Cole. Eagles 40, Chiefs 22. I'll keep saying it until you make it stop.
Cole: Five Super Bowls, Ray. Five. You have two. But America's Team needs to start winning America's playoff games, and tonight would be a start.
